analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 5289-6128). The patch shows only two head-side documentation changes: the 'Last updated' date at line 3 and one added troubleshooting table row near head line 3552, about a crash loop on a pre-release macOS 27.2 build. The base excerpts are unchanged context. The changed hunks sit outside the supplied excerpt ranges, so I reviewed the surrounding text only, not the new row's full content, which the patch excerpt truncates.

The surrounding text covers cluster prefill bounds, stage KV precision, SSD prefix record encoding, GPT-OSS/MiMo/Gemma batch paths and manifest pins. It matches the existing threat model and I found no contradiction:
- Cluster SSD prefix records are encrypted and sealed to an encoding header. This is consistent with T-041's KEK/HMAC posture, although the cluster-specific tier is not part of T-041's listed affected files. Cluster record authentication, lookup-tag derivation and TTL are not described in the supplied text, so I could not verify them against T-041.
- The doc says the encoding is sealed in the record header and a mismatched record is deleted, which fails closed.
- Mismatched KV precision across the two ranks refuses to load, which fails closed.
- Encrypted data-plane transport for large boundaries has no raw fallback.
- Manifest pin repair replaces manifest.json only when the fetched bytes name the same artifact.

Because this is a documentation-only change (a date and a troubleshooting row) with no code, control or boundary change, I identified no concrete security regression and no threat-model invalidation. Remaining uncertainty: the truncated added row's full text was not visible, but it appears to be a benign crash-diagnostic note. I did not verify the doc claims against source code.
